program: Business English — Corporate Communication in a Global Airline
hub_subtitle: Reunião regional, e-mail corporativo, treinamento global e convenção internacional

lesson.menu_title: Then vs. Now — The Status Update
lesson.menu_desc: Choosing between last Tuesday and so far, and what that choice does to a corporate email -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- Then vs. Now
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rosa M. Mitiko Shida | Lesson 3 -- Then vs. Now

listenings.text: Rosa, it is Paulo again. Two quick things before Thursday. First, I read your status update this morning and it was clear, so thank you. The only thing I changed was the last paragraph, because you wrote that the client confirmed the contract last week, and in fact they have not confirmed anything yet. They asked for a new proposal. That is a different sentence. Second thing: the figures for the third quarter came out yesterday and they are better than we expected. Your region is up nine per cent. I have already sent the file to your inbox. Have a look before the call, because somebody will bring it up.

Good morning. This is the weekly summary for the commercial team, and I will keep it to three points. Point one, the third quarter closed on Tuesday. We ended the quarter nine per cent above target in Brazil and four per cent below in Chile, and those are the final figures. Point two, what is still open. We have not signed the two contracts we discussed in August, and the client has asked for a new proposal in both cases. Point three, the deadline. Every account manager has to send the draft of the fourth quarter plan by the end of next week. Two of you have already sent it. Thank you, and please postpone anything else before you postpone that.

items.situation: Your manager asks when you sent the proposal. It went out on Tuesday.
tips: A closed day takes the past simple
I sent it on Tuesday -- not I have sent it on Tuesday

items.situation: A client asks how many contracts your team has closed this year.
tips: This year is still open, so the period is not closed
So far this year we have closed eleven

items.situation: Somebody asks whether you have ever presented at the convention.
tips: Ever and never live with the present perfect
If yes, add when in the past simple: I did it in 2022

items.situation: You have to explain why the third quarter figures were lower than planned.
tips: The quarter is closed, so use the past simple all the way
One number, one reason, one sentence about what happens next

items.situation: A colleague asks whether the client has confirmed the contract.
tips: Not yet is a whole answer
Say what they asked for instead

items.situation: The director asks what you changed after the last feedback he gave you.
tips: The feedback is a closed moment: past simple
The result is still true: present perfect

extra_audio.text: Paulo says he read the status update this morning and that it was clear. He explains that he changed the last paragraph because the client has not confirmed anything yet. Rosa says she wrote it after a phone call on Monday and that she will correct it. Paulo tells her the third quarter figures came out yesterday and that her region is up nine per cent. Rosa asks whether she should bring the figures up on the regional call, and Paulo says somebody certainly will.
